posts.text:
Rockstar officially brought back the legendary 6-star wanted level in GTA 6 and it comes with a brutal new rule.

In the video below, one player storms the Hamlet City Police Department, triggers full-scale chaos, and learns the hard way what happens when you push the law too far.

For over a decade, GTA 5 capped police chases at five stars.

Not anymore.

After holding off waves of SWAT teams inside the station and looting weapons from the police armory, the game hits him with a chilling on-screen warning: "Jason is now psycho. Refrain from extreme acts of violence to recover."

Minutes later, the sixth star lights up in the top corner with a blunt message: "You now have a 6-star wanted level. Escape is impossible, and the cops won't give up until you're hunted down."

No hiding in alleyways, no waiting out the timer, and no losing the heat once you hit six stars, it is a guaranteed fight to the death.

Within 30 seconds of triggering it, heavily armored tactical units breach the office and put him down for good.

Bringing back 6 stars as an inescapable death sentence changes how players treat open-world chaos forever.

Do you love that 6 stars means no escape, or should skilled players still be able to outrun the law?

posts.text:
I'm tired, guys.

I'm tired of the gaslighting. I'm tired of the bullshit. I'm tired of people falling for really stupid propaganda and damaging our country in the process.

The American right deserves better than another grifting influencer constantly mewling about why everything is hopeless.

I'm also tired of watching people who built their audiences on the right all of the sudden spend their time convincing those same Americans that everything they supported was a lie.

Trump made a mistake, thus the whole agenda was now a scam. He struck Iran, thus tiny Israel somehow owns our government. If someone mentions an accomplishment, instead of acknowledging it, it's met with whataboutism and 'you're an Epstien elite, a pedo protector, or whatever conspiracy theory is trending that week.'

But Trump also delivered on a lot with a major thin margin in Congress full of people who shows little interest in helping.

CPB reported 8,288 southwest border apprehensions in October 2026, which is 95 percent below Biden's monthly average. DHS and BP are reporting over 3 million deportations and 800k illegals arrested in under two years. Those are significant numbers that are being completely ignored by Podcastistan and the American left.

Substantial changes happened at the border, which Trump 100% kept his promise one.

Trump also signed tax deductions for tips and overtime. He promised working Americans tax relief and followed through on it.

NATO allies agreed at The Hague to spend 5% of their GDP on defense and related security needs. Trump pushed them to that agreement.

Trump also brought in $11+ trillion in new U.S. investment commitments, bringing back industry, energy, and SI to America. There are now 111 billion barrels of proven oil reserves under US control thanks to our actions in Venezuela. We have exported over 100 million metric tons of LNG. We are drilling like never before and Trump oversaw $1.3 trillion in deregulatory actions, which is the most in history.

Oh, and he significantly shrunk the federal workforce.

Those are all promises that Donald Trump made and kept, yet people that supposedly voted for him but now claim he betrayed them love to say he did nothing that he promised.

Tucker Carlson said that the election was a punishment for Trump doing the opposite of what he promised. Apparently the border, tax change, and the rest of the accomplishments I just listed were just nothing burgers, right?

In June 2025, Candace Owens told Piers Morgan that the decison to strike Iran belonged to Netanyahu: "This was not Trump's decision, it was Bibi Netanyahu's decision."

Was there any proof behind this accusation? Of course not.

In March 2026, Tucker Carlson presented the conflict as Israel's war. He cited Democratic Senator Mark Warner's assessment that Iran posed no imminent threat to America, then declared that Americans were fighting Israel's battle. You know, normal right wing stuff to propagate left wing Democratic talking points and push them as fact, right?

The Hodge twins' March episode with Alex Jones used chapter labels announcing that Americans would "DIE for Israel" and that "MAGA left Us" as they jumped fully into doomer Podcastistan mode.

Jimmy Dore and Owen Shroyer also did a show in March and argued that Trump had made an arrangement with the Israeli lobby (you know the boogeyman lobby controlling America, despite not being in the top 10 in either domestic nor foreign lobbies) and technology interests to pursue regime change in Iran. They posed it all as hypothesis, of course, because there was no proof of any of it actually happening.

Shawn Ryan asked Michael Lester on March 19th whether America was going to war with Iran for Israel, building the entire episode around a question that has only ever been a question, never anything answered with any semblance of truth. You can guess how that episode went, as it became a staple of Shawn's embrace of the Podcastistan doomer narrative.

Then Matt Walsh joined in and started pushing the same nonsense. Everyone that understood the reasonings behind attacking Iran was all of the sudden a neocon and a foreign shill. It was Israel's war. All of the lefty talking points that the right so gullibly embraced.

But what they all did was repeat the message that Trump betrayed his voters, that Israel controlled all of his decisions, and that Americans had been taken for fools.

So, let's talk about the Iran war without the fan fiction.

The State Department attributed at least 603 American deaths in Iraq to the Iranian regime. In January 2024, three more Americans were killed by an Iran backed drone attack in Jordan, under Biden. In November 2024, DOJ exposed an IRGC linked plot that included a plan to kill Trump.

Those families have a much better reason to care about Tehran than whatever Netanyahu wanted.

And that doesn't even consider all of the terrorist proxies Iran funds and directs to harm American interests throughout the Middle East and Northern Africa.

I absolutely supported hitting the regime's ability to kill Americans and choke off the region. The public intel on the nuclear program was messy, and no one ever established an imminent Iranian nuke (not that such intelligence would actually reach the public under any situation), but as of November 18, the US and three European governments were still warning that the IAEA couldn't account for Iran's nuclear material and inspectors were being kept out of the one place the world needed them.

Calling it a war of choice never explains the alternative. More sanctions? Another deal? Walk away? Every option has a price tag that most of you are unwilling to talk about.

Look at the map.

The “pivot to China” crowd should probably start by checking China’s fuel gauge. Before this war, roughly one-fifth of the planet’s petroleum liquids squeezed through Hormuz, and in early 2025, 89% of the crude transiting there was bound for Asia. The Gulf and the Indo-Pacific aren’t separate theaters—they’re stitched together by the tankers running the route and our actions in Iran showed them that not only can we run theater level operations, but we can also shut down any choke point on earth that we see fit and there is nothing anyone else can do about it.

That is an unmatched power that the US possesses, yet Podcastistan will never admit it.

Oh, and Iran also arms Russia, and though Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea aren't a formal bloc, ignoring their cooperation in our planning is stupid.

Oil is part of the argument as well. Brent dropped from $107.03 on November 3 to $91.84 on November 4. Trouble in those lanes reaches American wallets fast and then magically disappeared after the midterms, but did anything actually change in Iran from a month ago? No.

So why the price change? Because it was all setup on speculation and on punishing the Trump administration for acting so that propagandists could blame it all on the admin.

And of course we have to discuss the Israel alliance that so many idiots love to trash while knowing absolutely nothing about it.

How about we judge it by what Americans get from it. The Trophy active protection system on our Abrams tanks came out of a joint US-Israeli effort. The Marine Corps' Medium Range Intercept Capability pairs Tamir interceptors and Iron Dome components with American radar to protect Marines from aerial threats.

Anyone calling the whole relationship a one way giveaway has to explain those massive benefits we receive, not to mention the trade, tech, and other strategic reasons for the alliance.

Sure, you can scrutinize the aid and even scrutinize the conditions. That's how an alliance works. But two countries wanting the same enemy capability destroyed doesn't prove Israel controls America, and neither do fairy tales created over a hundred years ago.

Trump owns his decisions. Congress owns what it funds. Blaming a hidden foreign hand lets them off the hook and makes the entire problem undiagnosable, which is actually the entire point of the propaganda in the first place.

Then there's the antisemitism, and it's right there.

Criticizing aid, lobbying, airstrikes, or Netanyahu is normal politics. Claiming Jews control everything is something else, and that is exactly where 99% of the anti-Israel sentiment really comes from.

The Hodge twins' March 30 episode with Stew Peters had chapters titled "We Are Israel's B****! and The Talmudists Want EVERYTHING!" Owens promoted Der Talmudjude, a nineteenth century antisemitic polemic. Carlson gave Nick Fuentes an extended interview and a bigger audience, and Fuentes's views were already notorious.

The Protocols of the Elders of Zion sold the same story: a hidden Jewish power pulling every string. It was a forgery. It survives because it hands angry people an easy target. And yes, it was absolutely created to confuse and control illiterate peasants in Tsarist Russia.

But that's the woke right: Collective guilt, permanent grievance, and a secret system behind everything. Disagree with them and you're part of the system. Slapping a conservative label or some Christian language on it doesn't change what it really is, guys.

Treating American Jews as agents of a foreign government is disgraceful. If you claim to defend Western civilization, learn where this garbage came from.

And to the people who say my service was for Israel: I swore an oath to the United States of America's Constitution and none other.

I expect the people who send Americans into combat to explain the mission and own the results, but I'm sick of hearing our service reduced to working for Israel. It writes off the American interests involved and treats those who served like props in somebody else's conspiracy.

The Air Force says Operation Epic Fury flew about 10,000 sorties and hit more than 13,000 objectives in 38 days. Those American service members deserve appropriate credit for these monumental feats in an otherwise denied theater. They also deserve leaders with a strategy that turns military results into something lasting, because the June agreement collapsed, limited strikes resumed, and the regime is still standing.

Veterans disagree about this war, and we've earned the right to argue about it. But every time someone uses our service to sell a Jewish control conspiracy, I'm going to object. Show the evidence, or shut the hell up.

We have to stop buying permanent defeat.

Foreign governments love a grievance they can exploit. In July 2024, the DNI said Iranian actors were posing as activists, encouraging protests, and funding them, sometimes without Americans knowing who they were dealing with.

Remember, this was always the plan of Democrats and the left, and they did not even have to push it on their own thanks to Podcastistan: Dismiss every accomplishment, turn every mistake into betrayal, and call every alliance foreign control, and people stop expecting anything from their own country.

Meanwhile, there's always another episode to sell.

I want the right back to using its convictions. Name the failing policy. Explain the fix. Hold officials to their promises and give them credit when they deliver.

Trump and his administration should answer for his failures and the people who built audiences supporting him should answer for what part they played in destroying the right's momentum and handing a massive victory to Democrats in the midterms.

I refuse to outsource my thinking to a president, a party, or a podcaster.

The American right should refuse too.

It’s November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls, last in a long string of mathematical triumphs that would have been unthinkable not so long ago, and the proof fits in a tweet. 

The tweets where people show Claude the proof and claim it appeared in a dream or randomly in the arrangement of alphabet cereal come on cue, and we laugh for a few days at models freaking out, but it’s uneasy.

January 22, 2027. When someone tweets Fable 6’s claimed proof that P does in fact equal NP it’s utterly incomprehensible, nobody who reads it can make heads or tails of it but the models all lose their shit.

February 7, 2027 and someone claims that the halting problem is the result of a confused stance. 

February 9 and Goedel falls, this time the proof is so obvious that everyone in math, philosophy and physics slaps their forehead at once.

February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone.

It’s not until February 14th, Valentine’s day, that The Song is first played…
